key_insight: Pristine graphene flakes (GF) are chemically distinct from graphene oxide flakes (GOF): GF acts as a non-disruptive scaffold that organizes perovskite precursors and improves crystallisation, while GOF binds more strongly but introduces lattice distortions and gap states.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the right graphene additive can directly improve perovskite solar-cell efficiency and stability, especially in compositions with difficult crystallisation such as mixed Sn-Pb systems.
method: DFT calculations compared GF vs GOF interactions with perovskite lattices.
Machine-learning atomistic simulations tracked flake contacts with solvated nanocrystals across solvent conditions.
Spectroscopy and device tests linked precursor organisation to film formation, efficiency, and storage stability.
evidence_signal: The paper reports that GF improves champion mixed Sn-Pb perovskite efficiency from 21.5% to 23.7% and also enhances storage stability.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on perovskite composition and solvent environment, so GF integration should be validated for each processing route.
paper_title: Understanding Graphene-Perovskite Interactions: From Flake Chemistry to Crystallisation and Solar Cell Performance
